chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, the most beloved of my companions to me is the most pious, the most jurist, and the most retentive of our hadith; and the one of the worst state in my presence and the most detestable is the one who, when he hears a hadith attributed to us and narrated from us, does not accept it, is repulsed by it, denies it, and declares disbelievers those who follow it, while he does not know, perhaps the hadith originated from us and was attributed to us, and thus he becomes excluded from our Wilayah.'
ai.seo_question: What qualities make a companion most beloved to the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor and Major Concealment, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against the arrogance of hasty rejection, emphasizing that true piety involves discretion and deep knowledge rather than superficial judgment. This hadith underscores the Shia principle of *tawaqquf* (suspension of judgment) regarding the authenticity of narrations, ensuring that companions remain within the fold of Wilayah by acknowledging the possibility that a rejected report may indeed be from the Imam. It serves as a critical guideline for preserving the integrity of the chain of transmission during periods of political and religious uncertainty.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The most beloved of my<sup>asws</sup> companions to me<sup>asws</sup> is the most pious of them, and most understanding of the, and the most concealing of them of our<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth; and the one of the most evil of states of them in my<sup>asws</sup> presence and the most detestable is the one who when he hears the Hadeeth linked to us<sup>asws</sup>, and is being reports as being from us<sup>asws</sup>, but he does not accept it and is constricted from it, and fights against it, and disbelieves from making a Religion with it, and he does not know perhaps the Hadeeth is coming out from us<sup>asws</sup>, and to us<sup>asws</sup> is the link, therefore, due to that, he would happen to exit from our<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from abu ‘Ubaydah al- Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘By Allah, the most beloved to me of my companions are most restraining from the worldly attractions (sins), most knowledgeable in Fiqh (laws of Shari’a) and most secretive in our Hadith. Of the worst conditions among them and most disliked is the one who on hearing Hadith ascribes it to us and narrates it from us. Not only does he not accept it, also he abhors it and rejects it. He has made those who follow it turn to disbelief while he does not know. Perhaps the Hadith has come out from us and to us is ascribed and with this he will be out of our Walayah (guardianship).’”
